notApplicable.reason: no Merkle tree/root exists anywhere in this pipeline (grepped generate_witnesses.cpp, verify_witnesses.go, verify_orbit_accounting.py, round4_release.py for 'merkle': zero matches). The certificate is a flat TSV proved by canonical-orbit accounting, not a hash-tree structure.

no shard concept exists anywhere in this pipeline (grepped for 'shard': zero matches). generate_witnesses.cpp writes one certificate as a single file (write-to-.tmp then atomic rename); both verifiers read it as one sequential stream. There is nothing to swap, remove, or reorder.

certificateSha256/verifierSha256 in both verifiers' JSON output are descriptive telemetry, recomputed fresh from the file every run -- neither verify_witnesses.go nor verify_orbit_accounting.py ever compares a hash against a pre-declared/expected value, so there is no live gate to defeat by corrupting a hash field. The closest real analog is round4_release.py's regenerate(), which does enforce generated_hash != committed_hash, but exercising that needs a full C++ regeneration run (36s+ for Z_31 alone) -- out of scope here (read-only on generate_witnesses.cpp) and not part of keeping this suite fast.

MANIFEST-SHA256.tsv at the repo root is a static sha256sum-style integrity ledger and does include an entry for this certificate, but no script in the repo reads it back in as a validation input (grepped for 'MANIFEST-SHA256' usage: only round4_release.py's own file list and ROUND4-START-HERE.md reference it by name, neither one parses/enforces it). No live checker verifies a certificate against a manifest, so there is nothing to fool.

no resume/checkpoint mechanism exists anywhere in this pipeline (grepped the whole graham-z29 tool directory for 'resume'/'checkpoint': zero matches). round4_release.py exposes exactly three commands (verify/regenerate/full), each a single fresh run with no partial-progress state to resume from.
